87.title: S1-01
sections: “S1-01” (until September 2026 shown as “Variation 87”) is a living work by Nikolai Grigoriev. It turns a single life, the traces one body leaves without being asked, into an image, one day at a time, so that living can be seen and lived as a work of art. What death sharpens is attention: a life is worth this much once you know it ends. A dated state is written “S1-01, state of [date].” The work is one; its daily states are states of one work. Medium: software, lived time written daily by an unchanging rule, screen.

The rule and this certificate constitute the work. Any image, screen or print is an execution of the rule: evidence of the work, not the work itself. Whoever holds this certificate holds the work. Without it there is no work.

Each day, the daily signal of one living body is turned into one painting. The seed of a day is drawn from the name of the artist, the date and the day’s record together, by a fixed formula. Every day is weighed only against the days of this body’s own history that precede it; a hard day is hard by its own measure. The signals are entangled before they reach the canvas: every visible feature is driven by several at once, and no measurement can be read back out of the image. The same day always produces the same sequence of marks. Once a day has ended its inputs never change, and its painting never changes. The work never shows the present. A day is met only once it has closed and can no longer be performed for. The delay removes the audience. What remains is presence.

The work accepts the daily signal of a living body from any instrument able to provide the schema of Appendix A. It is bound to no maker and no device. The artist is the sole subject of the signal in this work, by his own consent. Keeping the signal flowing is the duty of its subject. An interruption is not a breach. It is silence, and silence is part of the work. Appendix A, the exact schema of the daily signal, is printed only with the signed certificate and appears on no public surface of the work.

Mortality is the edge of the work, the pressure that gives a life its attention. When no new day arrives, the work does not pretend. The last painting is held. From the second silent day its colour begins to leave. By the fourteenth the image stands without colour, and it goes on dissolving into the empty ground until, by the thirtieth silent day, nothing remains but the ground. The work is then empty, not finished. Any day that arrives restores it in full at once; the work returns as many times as the days do, and no silence is final. Silence is never declared from a stored record alone, only by the living programme itself, so a sleeping machine cannot show a false death and an instrument that has stopped is never painted as a body that has. Upon the certified death of the signal’s subject the last state is permanent and the work is complete. The artist’s obligations do not survive the artist.

The subject of the signal may end his participation at any time. A declared withdrawal, a signed and dated statement recorded in the provenance log, is written as silence from its date. The work registers absence, never its cause, and an undeclared silence is never named a death. Withdrawal acts forward only: the days already written remain part of the work.

The work keeps every day it has lived. Each state is frozen as it was written on its own day; the future never repaints the past. Recorded gaps remain visible as gaps. The archive is the work’s memory and its full body.

This certificate transfers the work; re-registration of this document is the transfer. The bond to the artist’s body survives any sale: this work is not re-bound to another body. If the certificate is lost, the artist may reissue it once, in person, recorded in the provenance log. After the artist there is no reissue.

The artist maintains the performing programme and one working signal adapter for five years from the date of transfer. After that the owner holds the complete rule, the code, the seed formula and the schema of Appendix A: enough for any competent technician to perform any state of the work again.
Unique, 1/1. Daily states are states of this one work. They are not numbered and are not sold separately.

archipelago.title: S5-01
sections: “S5-01” (until September 2026 shown as “Archipelago”) is a living work by Nikolai Grigoriev. It is made from the only hours of a day in which a person cannot pose. The rest of the time a life is presented. A pose is held with muscle, attention and will, and in sleep there is nothing left to hold it with. The instrument does not record a picture of the man. It records what is left of him when the pose cannot be held. Its subject is the part of a life that no one, including the one living it, is performing. A dated state is written “S5-01, state of [date],” naming the night that made it. The work is one; its nightly states are states of one work. Medium: software, a sleeping body written nightly by an unchanging rule, screen.

The rule and this certificate constitute the work. Any image, screen or print is an execution of the rule: evidence of the work, not the work itself. Whoever holds this certificate holds the work. Without it there is no work.

Each night of one sleeping body is turned into one painting. Every five minutes of sleep is one charge: its weight is the depth of those minutes, its radius the body’s recovery in them. The painting is the level set of their sum. While the body keeps returning, neighbouring minutes merge into one mass; when it stops, the mass falls apart into islands. Nothing decides whether a night is one body or an archipelago except the night. The hours awake are not drawn. They only part. Falling asleep occupies its true place at the head and stays empty. The light along the edge is the pulse of those minutes, read against that night’s own floor, because the heart is the one thing the body never switches off. The seed of a night is drawn from that night alone; the date plays no part in it. The same night always makes the same painting, and a night already painted is never repainted. The instrument’s own verdict on the night, its score, is used nowhere in the work.

The work accepts the nightly signal of a sleeping body from any instrument able to provide the schema of Appendix A: the sequence of sleep stages, the movement, the recovery and the heart, at the resolution the schema states. It is bound to no maker and no device. The artist is the sole subject of the signal in this work, by his own consent. A day the instrument recorded without sleep is not a night this work can paint, and it does not enter the calendar. That is not a gap in the record. It is the absence of the work’s material.

When no night arrives, the work does not pretend. The last painting is held. From the second silent day the edge goes out first: the pulse is the first thing to stop being visible, because it is the only thing that was never a state the body entered and left. The mass follows it, losing density until nothing is left but the ground. The ground of this work is the dark itself, present from its first night as material, so its empty canvas is that dark, and the work ends as a night with nobody in it. The work is then empty, not finished. Any night that arrives restores it in full at once, and no silence is final. Silence is never declared from a stored record alone, only by the living programme, so an instrument that has stopped is never painted as a body that has. This work counts its own silence from its own last night, never from the daily record of the same body.

The subject of the signal may end his participation at any time. A declared withdrawal, a signed and dated statement recorded in the provenance log, is written as silence from its date. The work registers absence, never its cause, and an undeclared silence is never named a death. Withdrawal acts forward only: the nights already written remain part of the work.

The work keeps every night it has lived, written once and never rewritten; the future never repaints the past. Recorded gaps remain visible as gaps. The archive is the work’s memory and its full body.

This certificate transfers the work; re-registration of this document is the transfer. The bond to the artist’s body survives any sale: this work is not re-bound to another body. If the certificate is lost, the artist may reissue it once, in person, recorded in the provenance log. After the artist there is no reissue.

The artist maintains the performing programme and one working signal adapter for five years from the date of transfer. After that the owner holds the complete rule, the code, the seed formula and the schema of Appendix A: enough for any competent technician to perform any state of the work again.
Unique, 1/1. Nightly states are states of this one work. They are not numbered and are not sold separately.

94.title: S6-01

The form itself is never drawn. Its subject is what a day builds, the shape a life would take if each of its days were given a body of its own. A dated state is written “S6-01, state of [date].” The work is one; its daily states are states of one work. Medium: software, lived time written daily by an unchanging rule, screen.

The brush is an oil brush on an ivory ground, with two palettes and three registers of stroke. 96.title: S6-03
sections: “S6-03” is a living work by Nikolai Grigoriev. It is made from the ground one living body crossed in a day: where it went, how it moved, how its heart worked. The days are laid on one sheet, and the sheet is turned by the body’s nights. A night calmer than every night before it turns the sheet clockwise, a faster one against, and the turns add up. The sheet is never returned to level. Its subject is the trace: what a day leaves once the place it happened in has been taken out of it. A dated state is written “S6-03, state of [date].” The work is one; its daily states are states of one work. Medium: software, ground crossed by a living body and turned by its nights, written daily by an unchanging rule, screen.

The rule and this certificate constitute the work. Any image, screen or print is an execution of the rule: evidence of the work, not the work itself. Whoever holds this certificate holds the work. Without it there is no work.

Each day, the ground one living body crossed is laid on one sheet, oldest below, newest on top. A day is laid down only after it has closed, at 09:30 the next morning in Barcelona. Each day adds to the turn of the sheet the turn of the night that opened it: a night calmer than every night before it turns the sheet forty‑five degrees clockwise, a faster one forty‑five degrees against, the middle night not at all. A day without a recorded night does not turn it. Each day is fitted to the sheet by its own reach; a day smaller than two hundred metres is not enlarged beyond that. The width of the stroke is the pace woven with the heart, each against that day’s own range, so that neither can be read back. The turn of a day can be read back as the rank of its night, and the path as a shape. A stop longer than a minute and a half pools the ink. The hour of the day sets its temperature, blue‑black at night and sienna by day. Ground crossed on earlier days lies as a dark wet bed under the stroke. The seed of a day is its date; the same day always makes the same sheet. A day that has been painted is never repainted. It loses a twentieth of its presence each day after, and never falls below a twentieth. A day without a walk lays nothing down.

The work accepts the daily path of a living body from any instrument able to provide the schema of Appendix A. It is bound to no maker and no device. The record is kept in the house of the subject and leaves it only in its public form: metres around a point in place of latitude and longitude, the heart as a share of that day’s own range in place of beats, the night as a turn in degrees. A circle of two hundred and fifty metres around the house is never written. No point inside it and no beat of the heart ever reaches the work. The artist is the sole subject of the signal in this work, by his own consent. Keeping the signal flowing is the duty of its subject. An interruption is not a breach. It is silence, and silence is part of the work. Appendix A, the exact schema of the daily path and of its public form, is printed only with the signed certificate and appears on no public surface of the work.

Mortality is the edge of the work, the pressure that gives a life its attention. A day without a walk is not a silence: the sheet is held as it stands, and the day is counted. When the instrument sends no day at all, the work does not pretend. The last sheet is held. From the second silent day its colour begins to leave. By the fourteenth the sheet stands without colour, and it goes on dissolving into the empty ground until, by the thirtieth silent day, nothing remains but the ground. The work is then empty, not finished. Any day that arrives restores it in full at once; the work returns as many times as the days do, and no silence is final. Silence is never declared from a stored record alone, only by the living programme itself, and only once the house has not been heard for a day and a half, so a sleeping machine cannot show a false death and an instrument that has stopped is never painted as a body that has. Upon the certified death of the signal’s subject the last state is permanent and the work is complete. The artist’s obligations do not survive the artist.

The subject of the signal may end his participation at any time. A declared withdrawal, a signed and dated statement recorded in the provenance log, is written as silence from its date. The work registers absence, never its cause, and an undeclared silence is never named a death. Withdrawal acts forward only: the days already written remain part of the work.

The work keeps every day it has lived. Each day is frozen as it was laid on its own morning; the future never repaints the past. The fading of a day’s presence is part of the rule, not a revision of the day. Recorded gaps remain visible as gaps. The archive is the work’s memory and its full body.

This certificate transfers the work; re-registration of this document is the transfer. The bond to the artist’s body survives any sale: this work is not re-bound to another body. If the certificate is lost, the artist may reissue it once, in person, recorded in the provenance log. After the artist there is no reissue.

The artist maintains the performing programme and one working signal adapter, the house that reduces the path to its public form, for five years from the date of transfer. After that the owner holds the complete rule, the code, the seed formula and the schema of Appendix A: enough for any competent technician to perform any state of the work again.
Unique, 1/1. Daily states are states of this one work. They are not numbered and are not sold separately.
